hypotheses.reasoning: At 20:22:57 payment-svc reloaded CARDPROC_API_KEY from the secrets store to version 18, and version 17 was revoked (#965). Starting at 20:24:24, payment-svc's card-processor calls fail with 401 invalid_api_key (#1046, #1113, #1149). The service is still presenting a credential the processor no longer accepts, which points to a rotated or revoked key not propagated to the running service. Every charge fails, order-service gets 502s from payment-svc (#1164, #1343), and api-gateway returns 502 on POST /checkout (#1091, #1208, #1290, #1392). The webhook-dispatcher 502s are downstream noise. Ruled out: no timeouts, GC pauses are small and normal, and postgres, redis and order-consumer logged no errors.
The card processor returned 401 Unauthorized. This is a fast auth rejection, not an outage, and it coincides with the key revocation, so it is less likely than a credential problem on our side.

verdict.recommendedAction: Restore payment-svc's card-processor credential: confirm that version 18 of CARDPROC_API_KEY is valid at the processor, then force payment-svc to reload it (restart or re-read the secret) and verify it no longer sends the revoked version 17. Confirm 401s stop and the /checkout 502 rate drops. Review the rotation process so the old key is not revoked before all consumers have picked up the new one.
